title: Measuring Bell non-locality in the presence of signaling
summary: Scientific inquiry seeks causal explanations of observed phenomena. The Bell experiment provides a paradigmatic case, revealing correlations between spatially separated systems that no local model can reproduce. Such correlations, known as Bell non-locality, are typically analyzed under the non-signaling assumption, which requires that local statistics be independent of distant measurement choices.
